title: 🦞 Discord plugin state corruption (similar to Telegram plugin) · Issue #12196 · openclaw/openclaw · GitHub
content:
OpenClaw 技术干货

1. Start with a working OpenClaw installation (gateway, Discord plugin functional).
2. Add a new provider (e.g., Moonshot) to the configuration via `config.patch` or `config.set`.
3. Restart the gateway (`launchctl stop ai.openclaw.gateway && launchctl start ai.openclaw.gateway`).
4. Send a message to the Discord bot.
5. Expected: Bot responds normally. [...] Correlation with Telegram plugin bug: Both plugins share the same runtime error and are triggered by provider additions or runtime activity. This suggests a framework‑level issue in plugin initialization/state management.
 Session persistence: Discord plugin stores state in session files; Telegram plugin uses a dedicated data directory (`~/.openclaw/telegram`). Both require deletion of state for recovery. [...] ## Description

Discord plugin exhibits runtime corruption with error: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`. The plugin can send messages but crashes when responding to incoming messages. This occurs after adding new API providers (Moonshot, ElevenLabs, etc.) or during extended runtime. The error pattern matches the Telegram plugin bug, suggesting a common underlying plugin‑framework issue.

title: 🦞 OpenClaw Cron Jobs - Building Proactive AI Automation
content:
OpenClaw 技术干货

Think of heartbeats as background awareness and cron jobs as scheduled actions. A heartbeat might check your email every 30 minutes as part of a broader context sweep. A cron job sends your morning briefing at exactly 7 AM, every single day, without fail.

## The Three Schedule Types

OpenClaw supports three distinct scheduling patterns, each designed for different automation needs. [...] The professionals who will thrive with AI are not those who ask the best questions. They are those who build systems where AI acts as a genuine collaborator, anticipating needs and taking appropriate action within trusted boundaries.

OpenClaw’s cron jobs provide the technical foundation for this proactive relationship. The scheduled task that checks your inbox at 8 AM represents more than convenience. It represents AI that works for you even when you are not working with it. [...] Cron expressions unlock the full power of traditional Unix scheduling with five field expressions for minute, hour, day, month, and day of week. “0 9 \ \ 1” means 9 AM every Monday. This precision enables complex schedules like “every weekday at 8 AM” or “the first day of each month at noon.”

Each type persists under ~/.openclaw/cron/ so your scheduled tasks survive restarts and system reboots. The automation continues working even when you are not actively using OpenClaw.

Schedule your agent to run tasks at specific times. Perfect for morning briefings, daily reports, and regular check-ins.

| `0 9   MON-FRI` | Weekdays at 9am |
| `0 /4   ` | Every 4 hours |

# Automations

 CapabilitiesAutomation

Automations are OpenClaw's built-in scheduler. The scheduler persists jobs, wakes the agent at the right time, and can deliver output to a chat channel, a webhook, or nowhere.

Manage automations with the `openclaw automations` CLI; `openclaw cron` remains an alias for the same commands.

## Quick start [...] Automation jobs, run history, and quarantined malformed jobs live in the shared SQLite state database. Use the CLI or Gateway API to change jobs; `cron.store` is retired.

Disable automations: `cron.enabled: false` or `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1`.

Retry behavior

One-shot retry: transient errors (rate limit, overload, network, timeout, server error) use a built-in retry schedule. Permanent errors disable the job immediately.
